mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has held in a narrow band near -30 for four consecutive weeks, indicating a stable commuting and errand-running baseline that will continue to support a flat-to-modestly-higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as no structural shock is visible.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged only -28.1 to -31.1 across four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean falls below its last-28-day mean despite TRANSIT remaining within a 3-point band throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (as seen from -9.1 to -20.9) reflects outdoor-activity substitution pressure (e.g., weather or restriction tightening) that pushes people toward indoor retail and recreation venues within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC in the week following a >10-point PARKS drop does not rise relative to the prior week in the majority of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both trend upward together, this signals a joint commuting-and-work-routine recovery that compounds to drive weekday retail footfall higher than either series alone would predict, raising RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -8.6 to -7.6 between t-3w and t-2w while TRANSIT rose from -31.1 to -28.1 between t-3w and t-1w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks in cases where both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rose jointly for two prior weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility below its recent average signals loosening of stay-at-home policy pressure or behavioral compliance, which frees time and willingness for discretionary retail trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3.0 percent for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dipped to 2.9 at t-1w before rising to 3.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following two weeks after RESIDENTIAL drops below 3.0, or if RESIDENTIAL remains elevated without affecting RETAIL_REC direction.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS exhibits a weekly oscillation pattern (improving then sharply worsening) consistent with weekend/weekday seasonal effects rather than a structural shift; this noise will not translate into a sustained directional move in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC shows a consistent directional move (not reverting) despite PARKS continuing its oscillatory, non-trending pattern.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls sharply week-on-week by more than 3 points, this signals renewed mobility restrictions or public transit avoidance due to tightening health policy, which will suppress discretionary RETAIL_REC visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -28.1 (t-1w) to -30.0 (t-0w), a decline of 1.9 points, close to but not exceeding the 3-point threshold
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks despite a TRANSIT week-on-week fall exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rising RESIDENTIAL and falling WORKPLACES indicate a compounding stay-at-home behavioral shift where people both sleep and work more from home, jointly reducing trips to retail venues and lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.9 to 3.6 while WORKPLACES stayed flat near -8.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL rising and WORKPLACES falling concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself shows mean-reverting behavior: the partial rebound to -9.6 at t-1w was followed by a reversal back to -11.7 at t-0w, suggesting any single-week deviation from the recent mean will revert within one week rather than persist.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC moves more than 2 points in one direction then reverses the following week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved to -9.6 at t-1w then worsened to -11.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC continues in the improved direction for two consecutive weeks after a one-week deviation rather than reverting.
